record_notes.DCP-LETT-13799F: Freshly read entire surviving single catalogue-summary block and footnote; incomplete original. Only Poor Joseph came back last night, having had teeth out is quoted Darwin wording; two arriving letters are editorial synopsis, and two teeth appear in editorial summary, not quoted clause. William recipient; arriving letters not proof Darwin read contents. Conjectured Sunday 1850–1854 spans previous period; Joseph Comfort rather than Parslow inferred from staff history. No exact day or period assignment, no complete authorial body or incoming prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1456: October 3, supplied 1851 ALS. Four body blocks, eight footnotes and bibliography. Emma trip postponed because baby ill, not completed Shrewsbury visit; workmen departed although later account payment October 27. Pear harvest and Exhibition visit yesterday, future William return hoped. P2 currently reading Liebig Familiar Letters on Chemistry; October 15 finished-reading log is later evidence, not full completion now. P3 personal advice and reference to prior oral talk, not preserved William written prompt. George drawings mentioned, not present assets.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1474: Tuesday 24, supplied February 1852 ALS. Five blocks, ten footnotes and bibliography. William school news letter explicitly received this morning; missing actual wording. Questions about steeplechase, form and master remain questions. P1 suggested message to Wharton is Darwin proposed wording, not an already sent William letter. Early-April visit proposed, actual March 24 itinerary later. P5 George money/read anecdote quoted by Darwin, not Darwin own preference. Footnote ages are editorial, not target prose.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1486: August 27, supplied 1852, incomplete surviving one-paragraph letter ending mid-sentence. William letter arrived Wednesday morning instead of Tuesday, giving August 25 under supplied year. Yard plan received and appreciated, but drawing itself absent. School placement praise and room/meal questions do not preserve original incoming wording. Do not complete terminal sentence or treat as full original.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1639: March 1, supplied 1853 inferred from notepaper and cobalt ink. Five blocks, five footnotes and bibliography. School note received this morning, source absent. Mumps comparison is historical family observation, not general clinical advice. Napoleon life already read, with older 1839 and 1843 logs in apparatus; recommendation is not newly completed 1853 reading. Crystal Palace building visit planned, 1854 opening remains future. Family news and affection coexist with observations, not excluded from persona grounding solely by genre.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1660: Wednesday supplied April 25, 1855 from prior-day account-book gift. Ten blocks, eight footnotes, bibliography and raw numeric markup inspected. Postal order sent/ enclosed, not William receipt. Pigeon house nearly complete, pigeons to be fetched next week and hoped breeds not yet acquired here. Raw HTML wire-net dimension is literal 1610 ft, without multiplication or fraction markup; hold numerical normalization pending authoritative witness. Salt-seed experiments underway, no results given. Crystal Palace visit already occurred; future railway hope distinct. Entomology rearing advice partly hearsay, Stainton reputation explicitly heard. Unknown gymnastic ladder remains unknown despite later apparatus.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1689: 29, supplied November 1855 from measles and visitor evidence. Five blocks, six footnotes and bibliography. School illness and recovery advice remain historical parental voice. Columbarian evening attendance and joining only planned; particular Southwark club is probable editorial identification, not explicit source certainty. Saturday pigeon return also prospective. Brent pipe interaction and hen owner prices reported; no actual hen sale at those sums. George optics already done, toys disappointing. Family and scientific pursuits overlap; worker family-rather-than-scientific framing must not exclude relevant pigeon evidence.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1340: June 13, supplied 1851, surviving copy. Three blocks, eight footnotes, bibliography and raw numeric markup. Bate drawings received and permission to cite unpublished paper granted; October appearance later. Source-complete Bate note/paper absent, but 1214 separately establishes manuscript reading before this. Prior-publication disappointment analogy and larval-stage assumptions historical, not silently corrected by modern editorial account of nonexistent second stage. Slide preparations used this day after two years, not simply future advice. Raw HTML micrometer amount 120,000 with superscript th has no fraction markup; keep literal source and hold intended 1/20,000 rendering rather than infer from flat text. P3 species caution conditional; no later synonyms imposed.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1345: August 18, supplied 1851, surviving copy. Five blocks, seven footnotes, bibliography, raw markup and actual proboscis diagram read. Note and specimens found upon return after ten-day absence; exact arrival not fixed. Actual inspection this morning, no transverse articulation seen; rupture and possible fold explanation is Darwin inference. Chthamalus not yet systematically worked out. Raw HTML 18 glass lacks fraction markup, so intended 1/8 lens rendering requires better witness. Asphalt obtained but not tried; recommendation rests on Smith and Beck assurance, not own tested superiority. P3 apparent internal tubular organ and labelled drawing support further proposed inspection, not proven anatomy. Ellis nomenclature rule and tenth/twelfth-edition tension retained with separate apparatus.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1471: January 10, supplied 1853 ALS. Four blocks, three footnotes and bibliography. Bate new residence and continuing work seen in Annals publication, not necessarily received personal note. Requests Verruca on noncalcareous and limestone substrata for comparison; existing few Devonshire specimens do not settle solvent hypothesis. Later results and 1854 published acknowledgment remain future. Metamorphosis follow-up question not an incoming response.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1511: April 1, supplied 1853 ALS. Three blocks, six footnotes, bibliography and actual MathML. Slate and Old Red Sandstone specimens received, observed no boring; still seeks limestone specimens. Bate many-specimen report and carbonic-acid suggestion conveyed through missing communication. Darwin believes solvent for Verruca, mechanical friction in other boring cirripedes; these are stage-specific views. Requests independent reinspection of complemental males, not completed confirmation. Caustic potash instruction has MathML numerator 1 denominator 4, one quarter hour, not fourteen hours; historical procedure not current advice.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1521: July 7, supplied 1853 ALS. Five blocks, four footnotes and bibliography. Missing Bate note reports Alcippe discovery; citation promised, not current publication. Limestone search still unfulfilled, specimens in next two or three months could help. Copies already made from two Bate drawings for early larval stages, attribution promised; permission assumed without fresh request. Earlier permission to refer to paper does not automatically establish specific copied-figure permission. Later printed plate references remain outcome evidence.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1528: August 30, supplied 1853 ALS. Three blocks, five footnotes and bibliography. Latest specimen inspected and Darwin considers it sufficient with previous facts to support calcareous-only action. His evidential judgment is not modern verification. Carbonic-acid reference now requested because previous Bate letter mislaid; does not prove original printed paper read. Lubbock oral report of related crustacean research remembered imperfectly; journal identity only imagined and later Quatrefages identification probable. Published 1854 distinction against Bate respiratory-current mechanism cannot be backdated into current request.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1214: Additional fresh full copy, six blocks, twenty footnotes and bibliography. Thursday between May 1 and June 5, 1851 from Annie death/return and later June 13 Bate permission, not any exact continuous-day composition. Darwin explicitly read unpublished Bate paper and drawings through Forbes, distinguishes previously published results and own unprinted observations, qualifies criticism and requests permission/specimens. Bate manuscript is not itself preserved as this letter. Copyist repeatedly Bates rather than Bate, original spelling unknown; keep witness spelling with separate identity. Prior anatomical literature read/verified versus recommended future Bate reading distinct. Apparatus modern larval correction and eventual October acknowledgment are later. Forbes condolence missing, not interchangeable with scientific manuscript prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-10366F: Additional fresh complete William incoming, six body/address blocks, two footnotes and bibliography. Cigarette purchase and possible size exchange, adult New University Club address and 1876 account evidence. XML artificial lower 1850 bound on before January 29, 1876 question-mark heading does not make it an 1851–55 school letter. Reject as prompt for any packet target on topic, date and life-stage grounds; no exact 1850 composition. Future cutoff and period hold retained. Vendor address is part of quoted letter logistics, not separate speaker turns.

visual_readings.visual_observation: Root viewed the actual black-line sketch. A broad upper outline narrows to a pointed lower end with several parallel strokes; an inner notched tubular shape bears the label (a) below a small opening near the top. It accompanies Darwin apparent internal organ in the probosciform larval mouth, not a proven transverse articulation or an independently observed Bate illustration.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
